authority: CEO R319 §P7 — the AI loop must learn

atoms.lesson: 1D hydraulic models are adequate for straight-pipe shunt geometry but inadequate for nozzle/contraction geometry. The FDA nozzle benchmark disagreement (72%) was because the 1D model cannot capture sudden-contraction losses. P-01's straight-pipe shunt geometry IS well-captured (16% agreement with 3D solver).
atoms.applies_to: Future cardiovascular candidates. If geometry has sudden area changes, use 3D CFD from the start. If geometry is straight pipe, 1D is sufficient.
atoms.machine_action: When building a new cardiovascular candidate, check if geometry has sudden contractions/expansions. If yes → require 3D solver. If no → 1D acceptable.

atoms.lesson: Flow-gated drug release in CSF is patient-population-dependent. Works for 79% of patients but fails for 21% with low CSF outflow. The mechanism is sound but the patient selection is critical.
atoms.applies_to: Any CSF drug delivery mechanism that gates on physiological flow.
atoms.machine_action: For flow-gated candidates, preregister patient-selection criteria (minimum CSF flow threshold). Do not assume the mechanism works for all patients.

atoms.lesson: Pore-size distributions cannot overcome r⁴ scaling (Hagen-Poiseuille). Small-diameter membranes cannot deliver clinically required drainage regardless of pore count.
atoms.machine_action: Before manufacturing a membrane candidate, calculate r⁴ scaling. If total conductance < CSF production rate, kill immediately.

atoms.lesson: Analytical optical approximations (diffusion, Kubelka-Munk) can disagree by 60-70% when used outside their valid regime. Monte Carlo is required for accurate tissue optics at small source-detector distances.
atoms.applies_to: Any optical candidate with source-detector distance < 10 transport mean free paths.
atoms.machine_action: For optical candidates, always run Monte Carlo (PyTissueOptics or MCX). Do not trust analytical approximations alone.

atoms.lesson: A clinically meaningful metric (safety-ICP time) matters more than raw drainage capacity. The drainage-capacity metric was misleading because a controller can preserve flow by allowing dangerous ICP.
atoms.machine_action: Apply METRIC_VALIDITY gate before any execution. Check: physical meaning, clinical relevance, comparator sensitivity, failure sensitivity. If any fails, redesign metric.

atoms.lesson: svMultiPhysics can be extracted from Docker layers via registry API and run with micromamba-installed MPI. No root access required. The hard blocker was an installation problem, not a science problem.
atoms.applies_to: All cardiovascular candidates requiring 3D CFD verification.
atoms.machine_action: Use the documented extraction path (Docker layer + micromamba) for svMultiPhysics. Do not declare EXTERNAL_SOLVER_UNAVAILABLE without trying this path.

atoms.lesson: Endothelial cells cannot survive long-term in CSF (no blood perfusion, insufficient nutrients). Future biohybrid surfaces must use CSF-adapted cell types (e.g., ependymal cells) or synthetic alternatives (glycan surfaces).
atoms.machine_action: Before manufacturing a biohybrid candidate, verify the cell type can survive in CSF-like conditions. If not, switch to synthetic alternative.

atoms.lesson: CSF flow variability (posture, activity, circadian) creates noise that fundamentally limits yield estimation. Signal-to-noise ceiling is ~18%, not 30%.
atoms.machine_action: For flow-estimation candidates, calculate the signal-to-noise ratio before setting targets. If SNR < 2, the target is unachievable.

application_rule: These knowledge atoms MUST be checked before manufacturing any new candidate. If a new candidate's mechanism matches a KA's 'applies_to' pattern, the KA's 'machine_action' must be executed before proceeding.
